elements.text: Attempted self-harm/suicide 34

elements.text: Confused, agitated or hallucinating

elements.text: Difficulty breathing, tight chest, or slow/shallow breathing

elements.text: Decreased level of consciousness 18

elements.text: Respiratory rate < 12

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected poisoning/overdose and any of:
elements.text: Having/just had a seizure 20

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected poisoning/overdose and any of:
elements.text: Excessive drooling/sweating

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected poisoning/overdose and any of:
elements.text: Shock1/systolic BP < 80

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected poisoning/overdose and any of:
elements.text: Pupils dilated or pinpoint

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected poisoning/overdose and any of:
elements.text: Persistent vomiting

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected poisoning/overdose and any of:
elements.text: Pulse < 60 or >100

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Manage and refer urgently:

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: First assess and manage airway, breathing, circulation and level of consciousness 16. If oxygen saturation < 94%, give oxygen via face mask or nasal cannula to maintain oxygen saturation ≥ 94%. Doctor to consider intubation.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If shock1/systolic BP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV rapidly, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If poison on skin (e.g. pesticides):

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Health worker to wear gloves, apron and surgical mask. If health worker/caregiver has any skin contact or contact with bodily fluids, wash off immediately.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Remove patient's clothes and wash patient with soap and water after emergency care given.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If poison in eye/s, immediately flush eye/s under running water or sodium chloride 0.9% for at least 20 minutes.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Ask about amount, type and time of substance ingestion/exposure. Examine tablets, packets/containers of suspected substance. If any of the following oral preparations taken in toxic dose in the past hour: paracetamol/amitriptyline/carbamazepine/phenytoin/theophylline/salicylates/mushroom poisoning/slow release preparations/digoxin/beta-blockers/NSAIDs and patient fully awake/cooperative or intubated, give activated charcoal2 50g diluted in 100mL water orally or via nasogastric tube. Avoid activated charcoal if patient swallowed petrol/paraffin/iron/lithium/ lead/mercury/arsenic/drain cleaners/alcohol/antifreeze/household detergents.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If pinpoint pupils, excessive drooling/sweating, excessive secretions, vomiting/diarrhoea, pulse < 60, BP < 90/60, organophosphate poisoning likely. Give atropine 2mg IV immediately. Reassess every 3-5 minutes. If no response (still has excessive secretions, difficulty breathing, saturation < 94%, persistently low BP/pulse), give repeated doses of atropine every 3-5 minutes, doubling the dose each time: 4mg, 8mg, 16mg, 32mg. If some response, give the same or reduced dose. Continue until secretions controlled. Suction secretions frequently.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If shallow breathing/respiratory rate < 12 and opioid3 overdose suspected, connect bag-valve-mask to oxygen and slowly deliver each breath with patient. Also give naloxone 0.4mg IV/IM4 immediately. If known opioid user/addict, discuss starting dose of naloxone with PIH. Reassess every 2 minutes: if respiratory rate still < 12, give increasing doses of naloxone every 2-3 minutes: 0.8mg, 2mg, 4mg, up to a total of 10mg. Naloxone wears off quickly, monitor closely and give further doses if needed.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If overdose of > 10g or 200mg/kg of paracetamol or symptomatic and referral delay, give N-acetylcysteine 140mg/kg orally, then 70mg/kg 4 hourly. Avoid giving N-acetylcysteine together with activated charcoal. Monitor closely for possible anaphylactic reaction5 after initial dose, assess and manage 28.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If exposed to carbon monoxide (exhaust fumes), give 100% face mask oxygen.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If no response, or overdose/poisoning with other or unknown substance, discuss with specialist or Poisons Information Helpline 200. Notify6 if pesticide, mercury or lead poisoning.
While assessing the patient, contact Poisons Information Helpline (PIH) 200 or consult AfriTox database (if available) to help with management and to calculate toxic dose.

1If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 2When mixing, add a small amount of water to charcoal in a container. Cap and shake the container to mix, then add the rest of the water. 3Examples of opioids include: codeine, tramadol, morphine, oxycodone, hydrocodone, fentanyl. 4Give naloxone IM only if IV not possible. 5Generalised rash, face/tongue swelling, vomiting, BP < 90/60. 6Notify within 24 hours (7 days if lead/mercury poisoning) via NMC App (download from NICD website/app store) or www.nicd.ac.za/nmc-overview/notification-process.
POISONING/OVERDOSE
Toxic dose
• Refer urgently. • Discuss need for activated charcoal with PIH 200. • If self-harm 34. • Advise to return if condition worsens.
Non-toxic dose and no symptoms Unknown poison or dose Non-toxic dose and has symptoms

Approach to the patient with suspected poisoning/overdose not needing urgent attention • Ask about amount, type and time of substance ingestion or exposure. Examine tablets, packets, containers of suspected substance. If intentional exposure to poison/overdose, refer. • Contact the PIH 200 or consult AfriTox poisons information database to determine if toxic dose has been swallowed:
Discuss further management with PIH 200.
